name: VitaCore LumiDerm Anti-Aging Dermal Renewal Array
body_location: subdermal facial and neck (standard); optional full-body extension panels
description:
The LumiDerm is a bioactive subdermal array installed across the face and neck that continuously mediates the skin's natural aging processes at the cellular level. A network of nanoscale bioreactors embedded in the dermal layer delivers precisely metered concentrations of collagen synthesis stimulants, elastin precursors, ceramide analogs, and localized anti-inflammatory compounds, maintaining the structural integrity of the dermis without surgical intervention. The system also includes a mild melanin redistribution function that gradually resolves existing hyperpigmentation, sun damage, and uneven tone, and a microvasculature support layer that sustains healthy capillary density — the underlying cause of the dull, sallow appearance associated with aging. Unlike earlier generations of cosmetic dermal implants, the LumiDerm does not freeze or alter facial movement; it works with the skin's natural mechanics, maintaining elasticity rather than rigidity. A small subcutaneous reservoir at the clavicle stores active compounds and is refilled annually via a simple injection at any VitaCore clinic or partner pharmacy.

The LumiDerm sits at a culturally interesting intersection: it is priced accessibly enough for Tier 2 consumers to afford over a payment plan, but its effects are dramatic enough that it functions as a visible class signal. In GLMZ's workforce, where age discrimination in hiring is technically illegal but practically rampant, many Tier 2 workers in their forties and fifties view LumiDerm not as vanity but as economic survival — a necessary investment to remain competitive in a job market that reads physical age as a proxy for obsolescence. Younger users in their twenties and thirties increasingly install it prophylactically, the equivalent of sunscreen in a previous era. VitaCore markets it with the tagline 'Your face, maintained' — deliberately clinical, deliberately un-vain — to appeal to consumers who would resist a product framed as cosmetic but embrace one framed as maintenance.
installation_requirements: Licensed cosmetic clinic or VitaCore partner medical center; facial mapping scan required prior to installation; 3-4 hour outpatient procedure under local anesthetic
maintenance: Annual compound reservoir refill at VitaCore clinic or partner pharmacy (injection, 10 minutes); biannual bioreactor calibration scan; full array replacement recommended every 12-15 years

side_effects: Mild facial flushing for 2-4 weeks during initial bioreactor activation as microvasculature support layer establishes
Some users report skin feeling 'too smooth' initially — a tactile uncanniness that resolves as the nervous system habituates
Rare: localized over-correction in high-movement areas (laugh lines, brow furrows) producing temporary slight stiffness, corrected by dosage calibration
Annual refill injections occasionally cause 24-48 hours of mild localized swelling at the clavicular reservoir site
cultural_context: The LumiDerm has collapsed what was once a clear generational divide in cosmetic cyberware adoption. Older generations in GLMZ remember when anti-aging treatments were expensive surgical procedures available only to Tier 4 and above — the preserve of corporate executives and Spire residents who could afford the repeated interventions. The LumiDerm's payment plan accessibility has democratized youthful appearance in a way that has generated significant cultural friction. On one side, there is a genuine liberation narrative: workers who previously aged out of employment opportunities now have more runway. On the other, critics argue that affordable anti-aging implants have simply extended the expectation of youth, raising the floor of what is considered 'presentable' rather than creating genuine equity. Among Tier 1 communities who cannot afford even the payment plan, the visible gap between LumiDerm users and non-users has become a new class marker — the un-smoothed face read, unfairly, as poverty and neglect rather than choice.
known_users: Tier 2-3 workers in age-competitive industries (media, hospitality, corporate services)
Younger users installing prophylactically in their 20s-30s
Tier 4 users as a baseline maintenance implant alongside more premium treatments
Anyone navigating a hiring market that penalizes visible age
story_hooks: VitaCore's annual refill compound has been quietly reformulated, and a subset of long-term LumiDerm users are experiencing an unexpected side effect: the bioreactors are beginning to redistribute melanin in ways that are subtly but noticeably altering facial features — and VitaCore's legal team is already working on waiver language

A Tier 1 community organizer is building a case against an employer for age discrimination, but the evidence is complicated by the fact that the discriminatory hiring manager cannot tell which applicants are 50 and which are 35 — the case hinges on internal communications the players need to extract

A LumiDerm black-market refill compound is circulating on the Shelf at a fraction of the clinic price — but it contains an unlicensed compound that produces dramatic short-term results and catastrophic long-term dermal breakdown, and someone is manufacturing it in volume
